"Port the n=512 PANEL to CUTLASS CuTe DSL — the one tool the fleet has never used (all prior work is Triton or hand-WMMA); operator explicitly recommended CuTe for 'more control'. Rationale: Triton is provably the wall on the panel (can't sub-tile a resident panel: smem-OOM at n>=512 + tl.dot K>=16 floor) → panel stuck at 11.6% occ / 255 regs / 2-blocks-per-SM, register-bound on its serial reflector chain (biggest unworked n512 sub-kernel, ~47% of dominant shape). CuTe gives explicit register/smem/warp control: (1) smem-stage the reflector chain with tight register footprint to pack more matrices' panels per SM (lift 11.6% occ; note plain Triton de-spill LOST under B=640, CuTe smem-staging is a different mechanism, gate on measured occ AND time); (2) warp-specialize per-step norm/scale/update to shorten critical path; (3) optionally persistent producer-consumer overlapping panel(k+1) with trailing(k) — W2 brief-25's look-ahead was NEVER BUILT. Profile-gate each. Build CuTe via Python JIT; report toolchain blockers."

FOUR QUESTIONS:
1. Is CuTe DSL genuinely UNUSED in this run? grep the worker logs (autocuda/2026-06-22-09-10-03-qr_v2-optimize-tree-worker-*-log.csv) for "cute", "cutlass", "CuTe", "tcgen05" — distinguish actual CuTe-DSL attempts from mere mentions. (Note: worker 0's CURRENT brief-26 uses tcgen05 via hand-CUDA, NOT CuTe DSL — confirm these are different.)
2. Is the brief's claim sound that Triton (not the algorithm) is the panel wall — i.e. is there real headroom a lower-level tool could capture, or is the panel at a genuine ALGORITHMIC serial-latency floor that no tool escapes? The run has established the panel is "serial-reflector-chain latency-bound." Does explicit smem/register/warp control plausibly help a SERIAL-dependency-bound kernel, or is this misdiagnosed (the serial chain is latency-bound regardless of occupancy)?
3. Is item (3) — persistent look-ahead overlap panel(k+1)||trailing(k) — actually never-built? grep for "look-ahead", "lookahead", "brief-25", "persistent", "producer-consumer", "megakernel". If it was built and falsified, flag it.
4. Diversity vs worker 0 (n512 TRAILING via tcgen05 hand-CUDA) and worker 1 (n1024 trailing register-pressure). W2 = n512 PANEL via CuTe. Distinct enough? Risk: is "two workers on n512 (panel vs trailing)" fine given they're different sub-kernels?

Also flag the OBVIOUS RISK: CuTe DSL has a steep learning curve + JIT toolchain setup; a worker could burn the whole brief on toolchain/boilerplate without a measurable kernel. Is the profile-gate + "report toolchain blockers" escape hatch sufficient, or should the brief have a hard early checkpoint (e.g. "get ANY CuTe kernel validating within iter 1-2 or fall back")?
